item.title: US issues warnings against travel to six countries in the Middle East
item.description:
US issues warnings against travel to six countries in the Middle East

The US State Department has warned its citizen against travelling to six Middle Eastern countries, including Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Libya, Syria and Yemen.

In a post on X, the department said all six countries remained under its highest travel advisory, Level 4, which instructs Americans not to travel for any reason.

"We assign Level 4 based on local conditions and/or our limited ability to help Americans there," it said. "These places are dangerous. Do not go for any reason."

US officials said they would seek a “final end” to the war between Russia and Ukraine, beginning with trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday in the first substantive negotiations between the two countries since February.

The talks are also the first since the US launched joint strikes with Israel against Iran, and they follow bruising midterm elections that have weakened Donald Trump at home.

item.title: Trump says war on Iran could be 'ending fairly soon', but warned that US is 'locked and loaded'
item.description:
Trump says war on Iran could be 'ending fairly soon', but warned that US is 'locked and loaded'

US President Donald Trump suggested that the war on Iran could end "fairly soon", but warned that the US is militarily "locked and loaded".

"We’re seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it’s going to be ending fairly soon," he said during a news conference. 

Trump expressed that Tehran was "talking very politely", but reiterated that its forces are ready to strike. 

"I don’t guarantee anything. But if we do have to go back in, we are locked and loaded and ready to go," the US president said.

item.title: Iran was behind cyber-attack on French supermarket freezers, Paris says
item.description:
French foreign minister vows European sanctions against Tehran over ‘unprecedented’ hacks last month

France has said Iran was responsible for a massive cyber-attack on supermarket freezers and chiller cabinets that was described by its foreign minister as being an act of “unprecedented scale and unprecedented aggression”.

Jean-Noël Barrot said “Europe-wide sanctions” would be imposed against those responsible, adding that the attacks – which took control of digital thermostats to push temperatures up to above 50C – constituted “a major violation of the nation’s interests”.
